children.text: oṃ mano hi dvividhaṃ proktaṃ śuddhaṃ cāśuddham eva ca
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ</s>. The mind is indeed declared to be of two kinds: pure and impure.

children.text: aśuddhaṃ kāmasaṃkalpaṃ śuddhaṃ kāmavivarjitam ||
children.translated_text: It is impure when occupied with desire, and pure when devoid of desire.

children.text: mana eva manuṣyāṇāṃ kāraṇaṃ bandhamokṣayoḥ
children.translated_text: The mind alone is the cause of bondage and liberation for human beings.

children.text: bandhāya viṣayāsaktaṃ muktyai nirviṣayaṃ smṛtam ||
children.translated_text: Attached to objects, it leads to bondage; free from objects, it is remembered as leading to liberation.

children.text: yato nirviṣayasyāsya manaso muktir iṣyate
children.translated_text: Since liberation is desired for this mind when it is free from objects,

children.text: tasmān nirviṣayaṃ nityaṃ manaḥ kāryaṃ mumukṣuṇā ||
children.translated_text: a seeker of liberation must therefore always make the mind free from objects.

children.text: nirastaviṣayāsaṅgaṃ saṃniruddhaṃ mano hṛdi
children.translated_text: When the mind has cast off attachment to objects and is completely restrained within the heart,

children.text: yadā yāty unmanībhāvaṃ tadā tat paramamadam ||
children.translated_text: and passes into the state of <s>unmanī</s> (being beyond mind), then it reaches the supreme state.

children.text: tāvad eva niroddhavyaṃ yāvaddhṛdi gataṃ kṣayam
children.translated_text: It is to be restrained only until it reaches dissolution in the heart.

children.text: etaj jñānaṃ ca mokṣaṃ ca ato 'nyo granthavistaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: This is knowledge and liberation; anything beyond this is merely an elaboration of books.

children.text: naiva cintyaṃ na cācintyam acintyaṃ cintyam eva ca
children.translated_text: It is neither thinkable nor unthinkable; though inconceivable, it is precisely to be contemplated.

children.text: pakṣapātavinirmuktaṃ brahma sampadyate tadā ||
children.translated_text: When one is freed from adherence to either side, one then becomes <s>brahman</s>.

children.text: svareṇa saṃdhayed yogam asvaraṃ bhāvayet param
children.translated_text: One should unite <s>yoga</s> by means of sound and contemplate the supreme as soundless.

children.text: asvareṇa hi bhāvena bhāvo nābhāva iṣyate ||
children.translated_text: For through contemplation of the soundless, being—not non-being—is intended.

children.text: tad eva niṣkalaṃ brahma nirvikalpaṃ nirañjanam
children.translated_text: That itself is the partless, distinctionless, stainless <s>brahman</s>.

children.text: tad brahmāham iti jñātvā brahma sampadyate dhruvam ||
children.translated_text: Knowing, “I am that <s>brahman</s>,” one assuredly becomes <s>brahman</s>.

children.text: nirvikalpam anantaṃ ca hetudṛṣṭāntavarjitam
children.translated_text: It is free from distinctions and infinite, devoid of cause or analogy.

children.text: aprameyam anādyaṃ ca jñātvā ca paramaṃ śivam ||
children.translated_text: Having known the supreme <s>Śiva</s> as immeasurable and beginningless, one realizes:

children.text: na nirodho na cotpattir na vandyo na ca śāsanam
children.translated_text: There is no cessation and no origination, none to be worshipped, and no injunction.

children.text: na mumukṣā na muktiś ca ity eṣā paramārthatā ||
children.translated_text: There is no desire for liberation and no liberation—this is the ultimate truth.

children.text: eka evātmā mantavyo jāgratsvapnasuṣuptiṣu
children.translated_text: The one and same self should be understood in waking, dream, and deep sleep.

children.text: sthānatrayād vyatītasya punarjanma na vidyate ||
children.translated_text: For one who has passed beyond the three states, there is no rebirth.

children.text: eka eva hi bhūtātmā bhūte bhūte vyavasthitaḥ
children.translated_text: The one embodied self abides in each and every being.

children.text: ekadhā bahudhā caiva dṛśyate jalacandravat ||
children.translated_text: Though one, it is seen as many, like the moon reflected in water.

children.text: ghaṭasaṃbhṛtam ākāśaṃ līyamāne ghaṭe yathā
children.translated_text: Just as space enclosed within a pot remains when the pot dissolves,

children.text: ghaṭo līyeta nākāśaṃ tadvaj jīvo ghaṭopamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the pot may dissolve, but not the space; likewise, the living being is comparable to the pot.

children.text: ghaṭavad vividhākāraṃ bhidyamānaṃ punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: Like pots, the diverse forms are broken again and again.

children.text: tadbhagnaṃ na ca jānāti sa jānāti ca nityaśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: It does not know that brokenness, yet it remains the eternal knower.

children.text: śabdamāyāvṛto yāvat tāvat tiṣṭhati puṣkare
children.translated_text: As long as it is covered by the illusion made of sound, it remains in the lotus.

children.text: bhinne tamasi caikatvam ekam evānupaśyati ||
children.translated_text: When the darkness is broken, it beholds unity—the one alone.

children.text: śabdākṣaraṃ paraṃ brahma yasmin kṣīṇe yad akṣaram
children.translated_text: The syllable as sound is <s>brahman</s>; when it has faded, what remains imperishable is the supreme.

children.text: tad vidvān akṣaraṃ dhyāyed yadīcchecchāntim ātmanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Knowing that imperishable reality, the wise person should meditate upon it if desiring peace for the self.

children.text: dve vidye veditavye tu śabdabrahma paraṃ ca yat
children.translated_text: Two kinds of knowledge are to be known: the <s>brahman</s> consisting of sound and that which is supreme.

children.text: śabdabrahmaṇi niṣṇātaḥ paraṃ brahmādhigacchati ||
children.translated_text: One who is thoroughly versed in the <s>brahman</s> consisting of sound attains the supreme <s>brahman</s>.

children.text: grantham abhyasya medhāvī jñānavijñānatattvataḥ
children.translated_text: Having studied a book, an intelligent person intent upon the true nature of knowledge and realization

children.text: palālam iva dhānyārthī tyajed grantham aśeṣataḥ ||
children.translated_text: should discard the entire book, just as one seeking grain discards the straw.

children.text: gavām anekavarṇānāṃ kṣīrasyāpy ekavarṇatā
children.translated_text: Although cows are of many colors, their milk is of a single color.

children.text: kṣīravat paśyate jñānaṃ liṅginas tu gavāṃ yathā ||
children.translated_text: Knowledge is seen as resembling the milk, while those bearing distinctive marks are like the cows.

children.text: ghṛtam iva payasi nigūḍhaṃ bhūte bhūte ca vasati vijñānam
children.translated_text: Realization dwells hidden in each and every being, like ghee within milk.

children.text: satataṃ manthayitavyaṃ manasā manthānabhūtena ||
children.translated_text: It must constantly be churned with the mind made into a churning stick.

children.text: jñānanetraṃ samādāya cared vahnim ataḥ param
children.translated_text: Taking up the eye of knowledge, one should proceed toward the fire beyond this.

children.text: niṣkalaṃ nirmalaṃ ca śāntaṃ tad brahmāham iti smṛtam ||
children.translated_text: The partless, pure, and peaceful reality is remembered in the thought, “I am that <s>brahman</s>.”

children.text: sarvabhūtādhivāsaṃ ca yad bhūteṣu vasaty adhi
children.translated_text: That which is the abode of all beings and dwells within beings—

children.text: sarvānugrāhakatvena tad asmy ahaṃ vāsudeva tad asmy ahaṃ vāsudeva ||
children.translated_text: because it graciously supports all, I am that <s>Vāsudeva</s>; I am that <s>Vāsudeva</s>.
